Fig. 9 Number and mean distance over time | Fig.10 shows the results for temperature. When µT falls below 7◦C or rises above 23◦C, dandelion number decreases sharply. This is because dandelions are transferred to the dormancy or hold stages at certain temperatures. The number is very sensitive to extreme temperatures, but only moderately sensitive to mild temperatures. The mean distance increases with µT up to 19◦C, where it temporarily levels oﬀand begins to fall at 23◦C. It has medium sensitivity to µT. | Fig.11 shows the results for wind speed. The number and mean distance have positive corre- lations with µW and σW and change drastically when the two factors vary. When µW increases, seeds are dispersed farther and land further apart from each other. When σW increases, there is greater variation in dispersal distance. In both cases it is less likely for seeds to land on other plants or exceed the density, making dandelion number rise quickly.
